newsitem.title: CUBA: Former Spanish prime minister plans Cuba visit.
newsitem.headline: Former Spanish prime minister plans Cuba visit.

text.p: Spain's Socialist former prime minister, Felipe Gonzalez, plans to visit Cuba, probably in the first half of this year, a Spanish Socialist Party (PSOE) official said on Friday.
PSOE external relations spokesman Luis Yanez was speaking to reporters at the end of a 10-day visit that included a meeting with President Fidel Castro.

"The trip by the PSOE Secretary-General (Gonzalez) could be of great interest for the future of Spain-Cuba relations," Yanez said. "Few political leaders have today so many lines of communication open with Cuba and therefore so many possibilities of dialogue."
The PSOE has been critical of the tougher line on Cuba adopted by the Spanish conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar that took over last year.
Yanez said he had told Cubans that the Spanish Socialists believed Cuba should advance with economic and political reforms, but without interference or external pressure.

Tensions between Spain and Cuba spilled over last November when Havana retracted formal approval for a new Spanish ambassador, accusing Madrid of interfering in its internal affairs. The row was smoothed over but Spain has not yet proposed a new ambassador.
